geography: World Bank countries and economies with a non-aggregate region and at least one published value in the series. Codes follow the World Bank registry, including XKX for Kosovo.
transformations: Rows are grouped under their source economy codes. All years within the observed series span appear. Null in JSON and blank in CSV represent an unavailable observation. Numeric values retain the precision returned by the publisher. Explicit zeros and status codes are retained.
validation: Each observation from the API for every non-aggregate economy, including unavailable years, was checked for equality with its entry in the separately downloaded official wide CSV release.

agriculture-output.name: Agriculture, forestry, and fishing, value added (% of GDP)
agriculture-output.definition: Agriculture, forestry, and fishing corresponds to ISIC (Rev. 4) divisions 01-03 and includes the exploitation of vegetal and animal natural resources, comprising the activities of growing of crops, raising and breeding of animals, harvesting of timber and other plants, animals or animal products from a farm or their natural habitats.Value added is the contribution to the economy by a producer or an industry or an institutional sector, which is estimated by the total value of output produced and deducting the total value of intermediate consumption of goods and services used to produce that output. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period. Note: For VAB countries, gross value added at factor cost is used as the denominator.

industry-output.name: Industry (including construction), value added (% of GDP)
industry-output.definition: Industry (including construction) corresponds to ISIC (Rev.4) divisions 05-43. It is comprised of mining, manufacturing, construction, electricity, water, and gas industries. Value added is the contribution to the economy by a producer or an industry or an institutional sector, which is estimated by the total value of output produced and deducting the total value of intermediate consumption of goods and services used to produce that output. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

services-output.name: Services, value added (% of GDP)
services-output.definition: Services industries correspond to ISIC (Rev. 4) divisions 45-99 and includes wholesale and retail trade, repair of motor vehicles, hotels and restaurants, transport, storage and communication, financial intermediation, real estate, renting and business activities, public administration and defence, compulsory social security, education, health and social work, other community, social and personal service activities, private households with employed persons, and extra-territorial organizations and bodies. Value added is the contribution to the economy by a producer or an industry or an institutional sector, which is estimated by the total value of output produced and deducting the total value of intermediate consumption of goods and services used to produce that output. This indicator is expressed as a percentage of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) which is the total income earned through the production of goods and services in an economic territory during an accounting period.

methodology.source: World Bank World Development Indicators. See each series for its national accounts providers and metadata.
methodology.classification: Agriculture includes forestry and fishing. Industry includes manufacturing, mining, construction and utilities. Services cover activities such as trade, transport, finance, government, education and health.
methodology.denominator: WDI expresses sector value added as a percentage of GDP. Its agriculture metadata specifies gross value added at factor cost as the denominator for economies designated VAB.
methodology.interpretation: The shares are retained as published. Product taxes less subsidies and national accounting differences can leave a difference between GDP and the sum of sector value added. Employment shares have a separate denominator, total employed people. A comparison uses the same sector, economy and year for both measures.
